sampling_recipe.summary: 40 targeted in seven strata, each filled mechanically with the first N eligible candidates of a named source in the order the source returns them (fixed web-search queries, the GOV.UK search API by document type and date, the arXiv API by category and date window), with listed fallbacks; nothing chosen or dropped for looking easy or hard; every candidate and its fate logged. Strata (quota): S1 short letters/memos/minutes from UK, EU and US public bodies, universities and NGOs (9); S2 resume/CV samples and templates, career-centre, Google Docs and LaTeX (9); S3 arXiv LaTeX papers and theses, short and long (7); S4 Google Docs exports (3); S5 Chrome web prints (3); S6 long Word reports 21-250 pages (5); S7 designed/annual reports and a booklet as unpromised controls (4). Eligibility: public curl fetch, no login or bot wall; URL and SHA-256 not in the corpus, docs, or holdouts 1-3, and not the same source or series; real text layer (>= 100 characters on >= 90% of pages, 70% for S7) and not a scan; no AcroForm/XFA fields; 1-250 pages, Latin script, not slides; resumes only as organisation samples or templates; per-host caps. The exact queries and date windows are withheld until after the run so that the set cannot be reconstructed from this file.
sampling_recipe.outcome: 24 of 40: the recipe's sources ran out before 16 quota places were filled (S5 Chrome prints 0/3, S2c LaTeX resumes 0/2, S6b US state reports 0/2, S2a 1/5, S1b 1/3, S4 1/3, S7b 0/1), mostly from bot walls/geo-blocks, form-field signature boxes and producer mismatches; no source was added after candidates were seen

converter_not_run: Nobody ran exactdoc (or any other converter) on this set: the collector downloaded, hashed and classified the PDFs from their metadata and text layer only (pypdf, pdftotext, pdfminer), and did not read any fix branch, plan or WP68/WP69 code
